subproblem.title: Bochner change of variables from the lintegral identity along a continuous injective map on a Borel set
subproblem.statement: Let d, P ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on ℝ^P and ν a measure on ℝ^d, let B ⊆ ℝ^d be Borel, G : ℝ^d → ℝ^P continuous on B and injective on B, and J : ℝ^d → ℝ Borel with J ≥ 0 everywhere. Assume ∫⁻_{G(B)} g dμ = ∫⁻_B ofReal(J(v)) · g(G(v)) dν(v) for every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞]. Then ∫_{G(B)} f dμ = ∫_B J(v) · f(G(v)) dν(v) for every f : ℝ^P → ℝ (Bochner integrals; a non-integrable integrand has integral 0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (d P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ν : Measure (Euclid d)) (B : Set (Euclid d)) (G : Euclid d → Euclid P) (J : Euclid d → ℝ), MeasurableSet B → ContinuousOn G B → InjOn G B → Measurable J → (∀ v, 0 ≤ J v) → (∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞, ∫⁻ w in G '' B, g w ∂μ = ∫⁻ v in B, ENNReal.ofReal (J v) * g (G v) ∂ν) → ∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, ∫ w in G '' B, f w ∂μ = ∫ v in B, J v * f (G v) ∂ν
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof ('Let μ_J := (H^m⌞B).withDensity(ofReal∘J). By step 6 with g := 1_T … H^m⌞G(B) is the image of μ_J (carried by B) under G|_B. MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map … and integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul …; both identities hold for arbitrary f'), with general measures μ, ν in place of H^m. Notation: ι : B → ℝ^d is the inclusion of the subtype B, ρ(v) := ofReal(J(v)) = (J(v))₊ viewed in [0, ∞] (ofReal r is by definition the coercion of r.toNNReal), and ν_J := ν.withDensity ρ.

1. (Measurable embeddings.) ι is a measurable embedding because B is Borel (Mathlib MeasurableEmbedding.subtype_coe). The map e := G|_B : B → ℝ^P is a measurable embedding by the Lusin–Souslin theorem, since B is a Borel subset of the Polish space ℝ^d and G is continuous and injective on B (Mathlib ContinuousOn.measurableEmbedding).

2. (A measure on B.) Let ν′ := comap_ι ν_J, the measure on B with ν′(S) = ν_J(ι(S)) for Borel S ⊆ B (MeasurableEmbedding.comap_apply).

3. (Claim: map_e ν′ = μ⌞G(B).) Let T ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel and put S_T := B ∩ G^{-1}(T) = ι(e^{-1}(T)). Since e is measurable, e^{-1}(T) is Borel in B, so S_T is Borel in ℝ^d (ι is a measurable embedding). Then
 map_e ν′(T) = ν′(e^{-1}(T)) = ν_J(S_T) = ∫⁻_{S_T} ρ dν (Mathlib withDensity_apply).
 On the other side, μ⌞G(B)(T) = ∫⁻_{G(B)} 1_T dμ (Mathlib lintegral_indicator_one), and the hypothesis with g := 1_T gives ∫⁻_{G(B)} 1_T dμ = ∫⁻_B ρ(v) · 1_T(G(v)) dν(v). For v ∈ B, ρ(v) · 1_T(G(v)) = 1_{S_T}(v) · ρ(v), so ∫⁻_B ρ(v) · 1_T(G(v)) dν(v) = ∫⁻_B 1_{S_T} ρ dν = ∫⁻_{S_T ∩ B} ρ dν = ∫⁻_{S_T} ρ dν (S_T and B are Borel and S_T ⊆ B; Mathlib lintegral_indicator). So the two measures agree on every Borel set, hence map_e ν′ = μ⌞G(B).

4. (Transport of the Bochner integral.) Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be arbitrary. Because e and ι are measurable embeddings, Mathlib MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map applies to arbitrary integrands (integrability and the values are transported together, non-integrable sides being 0). Hence
 ∫_{G(B)} f dμ = ∫ f d(map_e ν′) = ∫_B f(e(x)) dν′(x) = ∫_B (f ∘ G)(ι(x)) dν′(x) = ∫ (f ∘ G) d(map_ι ν′),
 and map_ι ν′ = map_ι(comap_ι ν_J) = ν_J⌞B (Mathlib map_comap_subtype_coe, B Borel). So ∫_{G(B)} f dμ = ∫_B f(G(v)) dν_J(v).

5. (Removing the density.) ν_J = ν.withDensity(v ↦ (J(v)).toNNReal) with v ↦ (J(v)).toNNReal measurable, so for the Borel set B and the arbitrary integrand f ∘ G, Mathlib setIntegral_withDensity_eq_setIntegral_smul₀ gives ∫_B f(G(v)) dν_J(v) = ∫_B (J(v)).toNNReal • f(G(v)) dν(v). Since J ≥ 0, (J(v)).toNNReal = J(v) as a real number, so the integrand is J(v) · f(G(v)).

6. Steps 4 and 5 give ∫_{G(B)} f dμ = ∫_B J(v) · f(G(v)) dν(v). ∎
proof_key_steps: G|_B (Lusin–Souslin) and the inclusion B ↪ ℝ^d are measurable embeddings.
Testing the lintegral identity with g := 1_T shows that μ⌞G(B) is the image under G|_B of ν.withDensity(ofReal ∘ J) restricted to B.
MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map transports the Bochner integral of an arbitrary f to ∫_B f∘G d(ν.withDensity(ofReal ∘ J)).
setIntegral_withDensity_eq_setIntegral_smul₀ with J ≥ 0 turns this into ∫_B J·(f∘G) dν.

audit.reason: Indicator tests establish the exact pushforward identity on the Borel subtype B. Measurable-embedding transport and the finite nonnegative density formula then prove the Bochner identity for every f, including nonintegrable cases. No global measurability of G or sigma-finiteness is silently required.

subproblem.title: Borel gluing of functions along disjoint injective continuous images of Borel sets
subproblem.statement: Let m, d ∈ ℕ and, for i ∈ ℕ, let F_i : ℝ^m → ℝ^d be continuous, B_i ⊆ ℝ^m Borel with F_i injective on B_i, and h_i : ℝ^m → ℝ Borel with h_i ≥ 0 everywhere. Assume the images F_i(B_i) are pairwise disjoint. Then there is a Borel J : ℝ^d → ℝ with J(v) ≥ 0 for every v and J(F_i(b)) = h_i(b) for every i ∈ ℕ and every b ∈ B_i.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m d : ℕ) (F : ℕ → Euclid m → Euclid d) (B : ℕ → Set (Euclid m)) (h : ℕ → Euclid m → ℝ), (∀ i, Continuous (F i)) → (∀ i, MeasurableSet (B i)) → (∀ i, InjOn (F i) (B i)) → Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (F i '' B i) (F j '' B j)) → (∀ i, Measurable (h i)) → (∀ i a, 0 ≤ h i a) → ∃ J : Euclid d → ℝ, Measurable J ∧ (∀ v, 0 ≤ J v) ∧ ∀ i, ∀ b ∈ B i, J (F i b) = h i b
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (definition of J: 'F_i restricted to B_i is a measurable embedding (Mathlib ContinuousOn.measurableEmbedding) … ψ_i := (F_i|_{B_i})^{-1} : A_i → B_i is Borel … J(v) := j_i(ψ_i(v)) for v ∈ A_i and J(v) := 0 for v ∉ ⋃_i A_i; this is well defined because the A_i are disjoint'), stated for arbitrary Borel weights h_i ≥ 0.

1. (Lusin–Souslin.) Fix i. ℝ^m is a Polish space, B_i is Borel, F_i is continuous on B_i and injective on B_i. By the Lusin–Souslin theorem the restriction e_i := F_i|_{B_i} : B_i → ℝ^d is a measurable embedding (Mathlib ContinuousOn.measurableEmbedding): it is injective, Borel measurable, and maps Borel subsets of B_i onto Borel subsets of ℝ^d. Its range is A_i := F_i(B_i).

2. (The glued function on one piece.) Define J_i : ℝ^d → ℝ by J_i(v) := h_i(e_i^{-1}(v)) for v ∈ A_i and J_i(v) := 0 for v ∉ A_i; in Lean, J_i := Function.extend e_i (h_i ∘ val) 0. J_i is Borel because e_i is a measurable embedding and h_i ∘ val and the constant 0 are measurable (Mathlib MeasurableEmbedding.measurable_extend: for v in the Borel range the value is (h_i ∘ val ∘ e_i^{-1})(v), where e_i^{-1} : A_i → B_i is measurable, and outside the range it is 0). Moreover J_i(F_i(b)) = h_i(b) for b ∈ B_i (injectivity of e_i, Function.Injective.extend_apply), and J_i(v) = 0 for v ∉ A_i (Function.extend_apply').

3. (Gluing.) Define J : ℝ^d → ℝ by J(v) := (Σ_{i∈ℕ} ofReal(J_i(v))).toReal, the countable sum being taken in [0, ∞]. Each v ↦ ofReal(J_i(v)) is measurable, a countable sum of measurable [0, ∞]-valued functions is measurable, and toReal : [0, ∞] → ℝ is measurable; so J is Borel. J(v) ≥ 0 for every v because toReal takes values in [0, ∞).

4. (Values on the pieces.) Let i ∈ ℕ and b ∈ B_i, and put v := F_i(b) ∈ A_i. For j ≠ i, v ∉ A_j because A_i ∩ A_j = ∅, so J_j(v) = 0 by step 2 and ofReal(J_j(v)) = 0. Hence the sum in step 3 has the single possibly nonzero term ofReal(J_i(v)) = ofReal(h_i(b)) (tsum_eq_single), and J(v) = toReal(ofReal(h_i(b))) = h_i(b) because h_i(b) ≥ 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Lusin–Souslin: e_i := F_i|_{B_i} is a measurable embedding with Borel range A_i = F_i(B_i).
J_i := extend e_i (h_i ∘ val) 0 is Borel, equals h_i ∘ e_i^{-1} on A_i and 0 off A_i.
J := (Σ_i ofReal ∘ J_i).toReal is Borel and nonnegative.
By disjointness only the i-th term survives at F_i(b), so J(F_i(b)) = h_i(b) because h_i(b) ≥ 0.

audit.reason: Lusin–Souslin supplies measurable embeddings; extension by zero supplies measurable piece functions. The ENNReal sum followed by toReal is measurable and nonnegative. Disjointness leaves exactly one term on each image, and the nonnegative-weight hypothesis recovers its prescribed real value.

subproblem.title: C¹ maps on an open set: Lipschitz on compacta, null images, rectifiable images
subproblem.statement: Let m, d, P ∈ ℕ, let D ⊆ ℝ^d be open and let G : ℝ^d → ℝ^P be C¹ on D. Write H^m := μHE[m]. Then (i) for every compact K ⊆ D there is L ≥ 0 such that G is L-Lipschitz on K; (ii) H^m(G(S)) = 0 for every S ⊆ D with H^m(S) = 0; (iii) G(S) is countably m-rectifiable for every countably m-rectifiable S ⊆ D (Simon Ch. 3, 1.1: S ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_k Ψ_k(ℝ^m) with H^m(M₀) = 0 and every Ψ_k : ℝ^m → ℝ^d Lipschitz).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m d P : ℕ) (D : Set (Euclid d)) (G : Euclid d → Euclid P), IsOpen D → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 G D → (∀ K : Set (Euclid d), IsCompact K → K ⊆ D → ∃ L : NNReal, LipschitzOnWith L G K) ∧ (∀ S : Set (Euclid d), S ⊆ D → μHE[m] S = 0 → μHE[m] (G '' S) = 0) ∧ ∀ S : Set (Euclid d), S ⊆ D → CountablyRectifiable m S → CountablyRectifiable m (G '' S)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 0(a), (b) and (d) of the parent proof (local Lipschitz bounds for the C¹ map G), isolated for an arbitrary S ⊆ D and with the details filled in. Notation: H^m := μHE[m] (on ℝ^d and on ℝ^P), |·| the Euclidean norms.

1. (G is locally Lipschitz on D.) Let x ∈ D. Since D is open, choose r > 0 with closedBall(x, 2r) ⊆ D. G is C¹ on the open set D, so G is differentiable on D and DG is continuous on D; hence ‖DG‖ is bounded on the compact set closedBall(x, 2r), say by L_x. This ball is convex, so the mean value inequality gives |G(v) − G(v′)| ≤ L_x|v − v′| for all v, v′ ∈ closedBall(x, 2r). (Equivalently: G is C¹ at x because D is a neighbourhood of x, so G is Lipschitz on a neighbourhood of x; Mathlib ContDiffAt.exists_lipschitzOnWith.)

2. (Proof of (i).) Let K ⊆ D be compact. If K = ∅ every L works. Otherwise the open balls B(x, r_x), x ∈ K, of step 1 cover K; take a finite subcover B(x_1, r_1), …, B(x_N, r_N) with constants L_1, …, L_N valid on closedBall(x_k, 2r_k). Put ρ := min_k r_k > 0, L₀ := max_k L_k and M_K := sup_{v∈K} |G(v)| < ∞ (G is continuous on the compact set K). Let v, v′ ∈ K. If |v − v′| < ρ, pick k with v ∈ B(x_k, r_k); then |v′ − x_k| < r_k + ρ ≤ 2r_k, so v, v′ ∈ closedBall(x_k, 2r_k) and |G(v) − G(v′)| ≤ L₀|v − v′|. If |v − v′| ≥ ρ, then |G(v) − G(v′)| ≤ 2M_K ≤ (2M_K/ρ)|v − v′|. Hence G is L-Lipschitz on K with L := max(L₀, 2M_K/ρ). (This is Mathlib LocallyLipschitzOn.exists_lipschitzOnWith_of_compact applied to the locally Lipschitz map of step 1.)

3. (Countable compact exhaustion of D.) There are compact sets K_j ⊆ D, j ∈ ℕ, with D = ⋃_j K_j. Indeed, if D = ∅ take K_j := ∅. Otherwise choose for each x ∈ D some s_x > 0 with closedBall(x, s_x) ⊆ D; the open balls B(x, s_x) cover D, and since ℝ^d is second countable (Lindelöf), countably many of them, B(x_j, s_j) (j ∈ ℕ), still cover D. Put K_j := closedBall(x_j, s_j), which is compact (Heine–Borel) and contained in D. (In Lean: the open subset D of the locally compact, second-countable space ℝ^d is a locally compact second-countable subspace, hence σ-compact; IsOpen.locallyCompactSpace and isSigmaCompact_iff_sigmaCompactSpace give K_j compact with ⋃_j K_j = D.) By (i) choose L_j ≥ 0 such that G is L_j-Lipschitz on K_j. For every S ⊆ D we have S = ⋃_j (S ∩ K_j), hence G(S) = ⋃_j G(S ∩ K_j).

4. (Lipschitz image bound.) If f is L-Lipschitz on an arbitrary set A, then H^m(f(A)) ≤ L^m · H^m(A) for the Euclidean-normalized Hausdorff measure; no measurability of A is needed (SimonGMT Chapter02 euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn).

5. (Proof of (ii).) Let S ⊆ D with H^m(S) = 0. For each j, G is L_j-Lipschitz on S ∩ K_j ⊆ K_j, so by step 4, H^m(G(S ∩ K_j)) ≤ L_j^m · H^m(S ∩ K_j) ≤ L_j^m · H^m(S) = 0. By step 3 and countable subadditivity, H^m(G(S)) ≤ Σ_j H^m(G(S ∩ K_j)) = 0.

6. (Proof of (iii).) Let S ⊆ D be countably m-rectifiable: there are M₀ ⊆ ℝ^d with H^m(M₀) = 0 and Lipschitz maps Ψ_k : ℝ^m → ℝ^d (k ∈ ℕ) with S ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_k Ψ_k(ℝ^m). Fix j. Because ℝ^P is finite-dimensional, the L_j-Lipschitz map G|_{K_j} extends to a Lipschitz map G̃_j : ℝ^d → ℝ^P with G̃_j = G on K_j (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_finite_dimension; e.g. extend each coordinate by McShane's formula); let L̃_j be a Lipschitz constant of G̃_j. Then
 G(S ∩ K_j) = G̃_j(S ∩ K_j) ⊆ G̃_j(M₀) ∪ ⋃_k (G̃_j ∘ Ψ_k)(ℝ^m):

 By step 4 (with A := M₀ and f := G̃_j), H^m(G̃_j(M₀)) ≤ L̃_j^m · H^m(M₀) = 0, and every G̃_j ∘ Ψ_k : ℝ^m → ℝ^P is Lipschitz as a composition of Lipschitz maps. So G(S ∩ K_j) satisfies the definition of countable m-rectifiability (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable) with exceptional set G̃_j(M₀) and parametrizations G̃_j ∘ Ψ_k, k ∈ ℕ.
 By step 3, G(S) = ⋃_j G(S ∩ K_j) is a countable union of countably m-rectifiable sets and is therefore countably m-rectifiable: the union of the countably many null exceptional sets is null, and the countably many parametrizations indexed by (j, k) ∈ ℕ × ℕ are re-indexed by ℕ (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion). ∎
proof_key_steps: A C¹ map on an open set is Lipschitz on a closed ball around each point of D (mean value inequality), hence locally Lipschitz on D.
A locally Lipschitz map is Lipschitz on each compact K ⊆ D (finite subcover, ρ := min r_k, the bound 2 sup_K|G| for distant pairs): conclusion (i).
D is a countable union of compact sets K_j ⊆ D (Lindelöf / σ-compactness), so G(S) = ⋃_j G(S ∩ K_j) for S ⊆ D.
The Lipschitz image bound H^m(G(S ∩ K_j)) ≤ L_j^m H^m(S ∩ K_j) and countable subadditivity give conclusion (ii).
Extending G|_{K_j} to a global Lipschitz G̃_j, G(S ∩ K_j) ⊆ G̃_j(M₀) ∪ ⋃_k range(G̃_j ∘ Ψ_k) is countably rectifiable; the countable union over j gives conclusion (iii).

subproblem.title: Injective area formula with the Gram-determinant Jacobian, and Borel measurability of that Jacobian
subproblem.statement: Let m, P ∈ ℕ and f : ℝ^m → ℝ^P. Let Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x (the zero map where f is not differentiable), e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1, and Jf(x) := (det[⟨Df(x)e_k, Df(x)e_l⟩]_{k,l})^{1/2} (Real.sqrt). Then (i) Jf : ℝ^m → ℝ is Borel measurable; (ii) for every Borel s ⊆ ℝ^m such that f is differentiable at every x ∈ s with Df(x) injective and f is injective on s, and for every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] (no measurability required), ∫⁻_{f(s)} g dH^m = ∫⁻_s ofReal(Jf(x)) · g(f(x)) dλ(x), where H^m := μHE[m] on ℝ^P and λ := volume is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^m.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m P : ℕ) (f : Euclid m → Euclid P), Measurable (fun x => Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k l : Fin m => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single k 1)) (fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single l 1))))) ∧ ∀ s : Set (Euclid m), MeasurableSet s → (∀ x ∈ s, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) → (∀ x ∈ s, Injective (fderiv ℝ f x)) → InjOn f s → ∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞, ∫⁻ y in f '' s, g y ∂μHE[m] = ∫⁻ x in s, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k l : Fin m => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single k 1)) (fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single l 1))))) * g (f x) ∂volume
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the Notation paragraph of the parent proof (normDet Λ := (det[⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩])^{1/2} and SimonGMT areaJacobianAt f a = normDet Df(a)), its step 4 (measurability of b ↦ normDet D(·)(b) via SimonGMT measurable_areaJacobianAt) and its step 6(a) (the injective area formula SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_of_injective_derivative with finrank ℝ^m = m and an arbitrary weight), isolated for a single map f. Notation: e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1; (e_k)_{k<m} is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^m (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.basisFun, whose k-th vector is EuclideanSpace.single k 1 by EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply). For a linear map T : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, normDet T ≥ 0 is Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet, and SimonGMT defines areaJacobianAt f x := normDet(Df(x)) (areaJacobianAt_eq_normDet).

1. (Jf = areaJacobianAt f.) Let x ∈ ℝ^m and T := Df(x). Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram, applied to T and the orthonormal basis (e_k) of ℝ^m, gives normDet(T)² = det Gram(Te_0, …, Te_{m−1}), where Gram(v) = Matrix.gram ℝ v = Matrix.of (k, l ↦ ⟨v_k, v_l⟩) and the coercion ℝ → ℝ is the identity. So normDet(T)² = det[⟨Te_k, Te_l⟩]. As normDet(T) ≥ 0, normDet(T) = (normDet(T)²)^{1/2} = (det[⟨Te_k, Te_l⟩])^{1/2}. Hence Jf(x) = normDet(Df(x)) = areaJacobianAt f x for every x ∈ ℝ^m (not only on s).

2. (Proof of (i).) SimonGMT Chapter02 measurable_areaJacobianAt states that x ↦ areaJacobianAt f x is measurable for every f between finite-dimensional real inner product spaces. By step 1 the functions Jf and areaJacobianAt f are equal, so Jf is Borel measurable. (Alternatively: Df is Borel by Mathlib measurable_fderiv, and T ↦ (det[⟨Te_k, Te_l⟩])^{1/2} is continuous on the space of linear maps, as a composition of evaluations, inner products, a polynomial determinant and the square root.)

3. (The injective area formula.) SimonGMT Chapter02 weighted_area_formula_volume_of_injective_derivative (Simon (3.5) for an injective regular parametrization in arbitrary codimension) states: if E, F are finite-dimensional real inner product spaces with their Borel σ-algebras, s ⊆ E is Borel, f : E → F is differentiable at every x ∈ s with Df(x) injective, f is injective on s, and g : F → [0, ∞] is arbitrary, then ∫⁻_{f(s)} g dμHE[finrank ℝ E] = ∫⁻_s ofReal(areaJacobianAt f x) · g(f(x)) dλ_E(x), with λ_E = volume on E. Apply it with E := ℝ^m, F := ℝ^P and the given s, f, g. Since finrank ℝ ℝ^m = m (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), the measure on the left is μHE[m] = H^m.

4. (Proof of (ii).) By step 1 the integrands ofReal(areaJacobianAt f x) · g(f(x)) and ofReal(Jf(x)) · g(f(x)) agree at every x, so the right side of step 3 equals ∫⁻_s ofReal(Jf(x)) · g(f(x)) dλ(x). This is (ii). ∎

measurable_areaJacobianAt gives Borel measurability of Jf: conclusion (i).
SimonGMT's weighted injective area formula with finrank ℝ^m = m gives ∫⁻_{f(s)} g dH^m = ∫⁻_s ofReal(areaJacobianAt f x) g(f x) dλ for arbitrary g.
Replacing areaJacobianAt f by Jf pointwise gives conclusion (ii).

subproblem.title: Gram-determinant chain rule along an orthonormal frame of range Λ, and positivity for injective Λ
subproblem.statement: Let m, d, P ∈ ℕ, let Λ : ℝ^m → ℝ^d be a (continuous) linear map and let e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 (k < m) be the standard basis of ℝ^m. (i) If Λ is injective, then det[⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩]_{k,l} > 0. (ii) For every linear Γ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P and every orthonormal family σ = (σ_0, …, σ_{m−1}) in ℝ^d whose span equals range Λ, det[⟨ΓΛe_k, ΓΛe_l⟩]_{k,l} = det[⟨Γσ_i, Γσ_j⟩]_{i,j} · det[⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩]_{k,l}.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m d P : ℕ) (Λ : Euclid m →L[ℝ] Euclid d), (Injective Λ → 0 < Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k l : Fin m => inner ℝ (Λ (EuclideanSpace.single k 1)) (Λ (EuclideanSpace.single l 1)))) ∧ ∀ (Γ : Euclid d →L[ℝ] Euclid P) (σ : Fin m → Euclid d), Orthonormal ℝ σ → Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range σ) = LinearMap.range (Λ : Euclid m →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid d) → Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k l : Fin m => inner ℝ (Γ (Λ (EuclideanSpace.single k 1))) (Γ (Λ (EuclideanSpace.single l 1)))) = Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin m => inner ℝ (Γ (σ i)) (Γ (σ j))) * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k l : Fin m => inner ℝ (Λ (EuclideanSpace.single k 1)) (Λ (EuclideanSpace.single l 1)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (Jacobian chain rule: with R_{kl} := ⟨σ_k, Λe_l⟩, [⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩] = RᵀR and [⟨ΓΛe_k, ΓΛe_l⟩] = Rᵀ[⟨Γσ_a, Γσ_b⟩]R), written with determinants instead of square roots, together with the positivity used in step 4 ('the denominator is > 0 as DF_i(b) is injective'). Notation: e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 is the k-th vector of the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^m; all matrices are real m × m matrices indexed by Fin m.

1. (Proof of (i).) Assume Λ is injective. The vectors e_0, …, e_{m−1} are linearly independent and an injective linear map preserves linear independence, so v_k := Λe_k (k < m) are linearly independent. The Gram matrix A := [⟨v_k, v_l⟩]_{k,l} is symmetric, and for c ∈ ℝ^m, cᵀAc = Σ_{k,l} c_k c_l ⟨v_k, v_l⟩ = |Σ_k c_k v_k|², which is > 0 whenever c ≠ 0 because then Σ_k c_k v_k ≠ 0. So A is positive definite (Mathlib Matrix.posDef_gram_of_linearIndependent; Matrix.gram ℝ v is by definition Matrix.of (k, l ↦ ⟨v_k, v_l⟩)). A positive definite real symmetric matrix has positive determinant, since its eigenvalues are positive and the determinant is their product (Mathlib Matrix.PosDef.det_pos). Hence det[⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩] > 0. (For m = 0 this is the empty determinant 1 > 0.)

2. (Set-up for (ii).) Let Γ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P be linear and σ orthonormal with span{σ_0, …, σ_{m−1}} = range Λ. Injectivity of Λ is not used in steps 2–7. Define R ∈ ℝ^{m×m} by R_{kl} := ⟨σ_k, Λe_l⟩.

3. (Expansion of Λe_l in the frame σ.) Fix l. Since Λe_l ∈ range Λ = span{σ_k}, there is c ∈ ℝ^m with Λe_l = Σ_k c_k σ_k (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun). Pairing with σ_j and using ⟨σ_j, σ_k⟩ = δ_{jk} gives ⟨σ_j, Λe_l⟩ = c_j (Orthonormal.inner_right_fintype). Thus c_j = R_{jl} for every j, i.e. Λe_l = Σ_k R_{kl} σ_k.

4. (Transformation rule.) Let Q ∈ ℕ and let Γ' : ℝ^d → ℝ^Q be linear; put H(Γ') := [⟨Γ'σ_a, Γ'σ_b⟩]_{a,b}. By step 3, linearity of Γ' and bilinearity of the real inner product,
 ⟨Γ'Λe_k, Γ'Λe_l⟩ = ⟨Σ_a R_{ak} Γ'σ_a, Σ_b R_{bl} Γ'σ_b⟩ = Σ_a Σ_b R_{ak} ⟨Γ'σ_a, Γ'σ_b⟩ R_{bl} = (Rᵀ H(Γ') R)_{kl}.
 Hence [⟨Γ'Λe_k, Γ'Λe_l⟩]_{k,l} = Rᵀ H(Γ') R.

5. (Γ' := Γ, Q := P.) By step 4 and multiplicativity of the determinant, det[⟨ΓΛe_k, ΓΛe_l⟩] = det(Rᵀ) · det H(Γ) · det R = det H(Γ) · (det R)², using det Rᵀ = det R.

subproblem.title: Lower integrals over G(M) split along a Borel partition of M up to a null image (G continuous and injective on M)
subproblem.statement: Let m, d, P ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^d, A_i ⊆ ℝ^d (i ∈ ℕ) and G : ℝ^d → ℝ^P. Assume G is continuous on M and injective on M, every A_i is Borel with A_i ⊆ M, the A_i are pairwise disjoint, and H^m(G(M ∖ ⋃_i A_i)) = 0, where H^m := μHE[m]. Then for every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] (no measurability required), ∫⁻_{G(M)} g dH^m = Σ_{i∈ℕ} ∫⁻_{G(A_i)} g dH^m.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m d P : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid d)) (A : ℕ → Set (Euclid d)) (G : Euclid d → Euclid P), ContinuousOn G M → InjOn G M → (∀ i, MeasurableSet (A i)) → (∀ i, A i ⊆ M) → Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (A i) (A j)) → μHE[m] (G '' (M \ ⋃ i, A i)) = 0 → ∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞, ∫⁻ w in G '' M, g w ∂μHE[m] = ∑' i, ∫⁻ w in G '' A i, g w ∂μHE[m]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 6(b) of the parent proof ('The sets G(A_i) are Borel (Lusin–Souslin …) and pairwise disjoint (G injective on D), G(B) = G(N) ∪ ⋃_i G(A_i), and H^m(G(N)) = 0 … lintegrals of arbitrary functions are additive'), isolated with the null image as a hypothesis (the parent applies it with M := B, using that G is continuous and injective on B ⊆ D). With G := id it also gives the parent's identity for H^m⌞B.

1. (Borel images.) Fix i. A_i ⊆ M, so G is continuous on A_i and injective on A_i; A_i is a Borel subset of the Polish space ℝ^d. By the Lusin–Souslin theorem (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn), G(A_i) is Borel.

2. (Disjoint images.) Let i ≠ j and suppose y ∈ G(A_i) ∩ G(A_j), say y = G(a) = G(a′) with a ∈ A_i and a′ ∈ A_j. Both a and a′ lie in M, so injectivity of G on M gives a = a′ ∈ A_i ∩ A_j = ∅, a contradiction. So the sets G(A_i) are pairwise disjoint.

3. (One inclusion.) ⋃_i G(A_i) ⊆ G(M), because A_i ⊆ M for every i. Hence (⋃_i G(A_i)) ∖ G(M) = ∅ has H^m-measure 0.

4. (Other inclusion up to a null set.) G(M) ∖ ⋃_i G(A_i) ⊆ G(M ∖ ⋃_i A_i): if y = G(x) with x ∈ M and y ∉ ⋃_i G(A_i), then x ∉ A_i for every i (otherwise y ∈ G(A_i)), so x ∈ M ∖ ⋃_i A_i. By hypothesis and monotonicity, H^m(G(M) ∖ ⋃_i G(A_i)) = 0.

5. (Replacing G(M).) By steps 3 and 4 the sets G(M) and ⋃_i G(A_i) are equal H^m-almost everywhere (Mathlib ae_eq_set), so the restrictions of H^m to them coincide and ∫⁻_{G(M)} g dH^m = ∫⁻_{⋃_i G(A_i)} g dH^m for the arbitrary function g (Mathlib setLIntegral_congr; no measurability of g is used).

6. (Countable additivity.) By steps 1 and 2 the sets G(A_i) are Borel and pairwise disjoint, and the lower Lebesgue integral of an arbitrary g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] over a countable disjoint union of measurable sets is the sum of the integrals over the pieces (Mathlib lintegral_iUnion). So ∫⁻_{⋃_i G(A_i)} g dH^m = Σ_i ∫⁻_{G(A_i)} g dH^m.

7. Steps 5 and 6 give ∫⁻_{G(M)} g dH^m = Σ_i ∫⁻_{G(A_i)} g dH^m. ∎
proof_key_steps: Lusin–Souslin makes every G(A_i) Borel, and injectivity of G on M makes them pairwise disjoint.
⋃_i G(A_i) ⊆ G(M) and G(M) ∖ ⋃_i G(A_i) ⊆ G(M ∖ ⋃_i A_i), which is H^m-null by hypothesis.
So G(M) = ⋃_i G(A_i) H^m-a.e. and the set lintegrals of any g agree.
Countable additivity of the lintegral over disjoint Borel sets gives the sum.

audit.reason: Continuity and injectivity restricted to each Borel piece give Borel, disjoint images. The null-image hypothesis identifies their union with G(M) almost everywhere. The pinned set-congruence and disjoint-union lemmas apply to arbitrary integrands; measurability of M is unnecessary.
